name: Thornplate Intimidator
description:
Offspring {3} (You may pay an additional {3} as you cast this spell. If you do, when this creature enters, create a 1/1 token that's a copy of it.)

Whenever this creature enters the battlefield, you lose 3 life.
assumptions: Used the keyword name "Offspring" for node C's pattern, since the schema document itself explicitly labels this exact edge-shape (`cost:{N} cond:token;paid_at_cast`) as Offspring — treated as given information, not outside card knowledge. The specific reminder-text wording ("create a 1/1 token that's a copy of it") is a standard-phrasing guess, not something the registry spells out verbatim.

E and F are two structurally identical `life-loss qty:3 owner:me` nodes both under D. I interpreted this as one printed clause ("you lose 3 life") that can trigger separately for each copy of the creature that enters — once for the creature itself (via B) and again for its Offspring token (via C) — rather than as two literal life-loss clauses within a single resolution of the ability. This is a judgment call (see below).
Assumed no additional supertypes/keywords beyond what's explicit in the nodes/registry (e.g., not legendary).
couldNotDerive: Whether E and F are truly two separate triggering instances (my assumption) or two literal effects meant to occur together in one instance of the ability's text — the flow graph doesn't disambiguate a single node D having two step targets from either reading.
Exact printed reminder-text wording for the Offspring ability.
The card's name (by design, not determinable and not to be guessed).
notes:
Confirmed real card via forge-model/data/thornplate-intimidator.txt: Thornplate Intimidator, {3}{B}, Creature Rat Rogue, 4/3, K:Offspring:3, Oracle 'Offspring {3} ... When this creature enters, target opponent loses 3 life unless they sacrifice a nonland permanent or discard a card.'

Mana cost, type line, P/T, and the Offspring {3} clause (packet node C: enters, flags 'cost:{3} cond:token;paid_at_cast;set=1/1') all check out — that half of the card is a clean match and the agent reconstructed it correctly.

The ETB ability is a decomposition gap, traceable to specific Forge fields that the edge data dropped or mis-resolved:
1. Wrong owner/no target. The real trigger's SVar:TrigGenericChoice carries `ValidTgts$ Opponent`, and both SVar:PaySac and SVar:PayDiscard use `Defined$ Targeted` / `UnlessPayer$ Targeted` — the life-loss (and the option to pay a cost to avoid it) belongs to the TARGETED OPPONENT, not the caster. But packet nodes E and F are both `owner: me` with no `target` flag anywhere on D/E/F. forgeTranslate.ts appears to default the life-loss owner to the card's controller instead of resolving `ValidTgts$`/`Defined$ Targeted` back to the actual targeted player, and never emits a `target` flag for this trigger at all. This is exactly why the blind reconstruction produced 'you lose 3 life' (self-inflicted) instead of 'target opponent loses 3 life.'
2. Missing UnlessCost escape entirely. SVar:PaySac's `UnlessCost$ Sac<1/Permanent.nonLand/nonland permanent>` and SVar:PayDiscard's `UnlessCost$ Discard<1/Card>` (the 'unless they sacrifice a nonland permanent or discard a card' clause — the entire point of the card) have no representation anywhere in the node/flow data. There is no `cond:` payload on E or F encoding an alternative-cost-to-avoid-effect semantic. This is either a translator gap (UnlessCost$/UnlessPayer$ fields never read) or a genuine SCHEMA.md expressiveness gap (no documented convention for 'effect happens unless payer pays cost X or Y') — worth flagging to SCHEMA.md's open-questions section either way, but given forgeTranslate.ts is the stated target of the next pass, start there: it needs to detect UnlessCost$ on a DB$ LoseLife and encode it, rather than silently emitting a bare unconditional life-loss.
3. Flattened modal choice. SVar:TrigGenericChoice's `Choices$ PaySac,PayDiscard` is a genuine choice between two alternate escape-cost types (which unless-cost the opponent is offered), reflected in the packet as two flat, non-combine sibling steps under D (steps.D = [E, F], both unconditional qty:3 life-loss). Per SCHEMA.md's own flow rules, two plain array entries under one step key are ADDITIVE (both happen), which reads as an unconditional 6-life-loss effect — nothing like the real single avoidable 3-life-loss effect. Should have been either a `{combine: 1, of: [...]}` modal group choosing between two unless-cost variants, or (more accurately, since both branches share the same LoseLife effect and differ only in the escape cost) a single life-loss node carrying two alternate `cond:unless=...` payloads. SVar:LoseLifeFallback (the plain `DB$ LoseLife | Defined$ Targeted | LifeAmount$ 3` used when the GenericChoice fallback fires) is likewise not distinctly represented — though that's subsumed under fixing (1) and (2) rather than a separate defect.
4. Agent's E/F 'fires twice, once per entering copy' theory (to explain two identical life-loss nodes) isn't actually supported by the flow graph — D has no incoming edges from B or C, so nothing wires the trigger to entrance-count. This is a reasonable but unconfirmed guess on the agent's part, informative (shows the ambiguity of two unwired-but-identical children of one root) but not itself a fix target — the real fix is items 1-3 above, which remove the duplicate-node ambiguity entirely by replacing E/F with either a combine group or a single unless-cost-bearing node.
